title: Jeremiah Chapter 38 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Jeremiah chapter 38 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Jeremiah Chapter 38 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Jeremiah Chapter 38.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 38, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Zedekiah the king giving a command
questions.explanation: Shephatiah the son of Mattan is mentioned first in Jeremiah 38:1 as one of the princes who heard Jeremiah's words.

questions.question: What does the LORD say will happen to those who remain in the city?
options: They shall die by the sword
questions.correctAnswer: They shall die by the sword
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 38:2 states that those who remain in the city shall die by the sword, famine, and pestilence.

questions.question: Who did the princes say should be put to death?
questions.explanation: According to Jeremiah 38:4, the princes said that Jeremiah should be put to death for weakening the hands of the men of war.

questions.question: What did the king say about Jeremiah's fate?
options: He can do nothing against you
He will die in the dungeon
questions.correctAnswer: He can do nothing against you
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 38:5, Zedekiah the king states that he cannot do anything against the princes regarding Jeremiah.

questions.question: What was the condition of the dungeon where Jeremiah was cast?
options: There was no water, but mire
questions.correctAnswer: There was no water, but mire
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 38:6 describes the dungeon as having no water but mire, indicating it was a very unpleasant place.

questions.question: Who heard about Jeremiah being in the dungeon?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 38:7 states that Ebedmelech the Ethiopian heard that Jeremiah had been put in the dungeon.

questions.question: What did Ebedmelech tell the king about Jeremiah?
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 38:9, Ebedmelech states that Jeremiah is like to die for hunger in the dungeon.

questions.question: How many men did the king command Ebedmelech to take with him to rescue Jeremiah?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 38:10 records that the king commanded Ebedmelech to take thirty men with him to rescue Jeremiah.

questions.question: What was Jeremiah's role in the city?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah is referred to as the prophet in Jeremiah 38:9 when Ebedmelech speaks to the king about him.

questions.question: What did the princes accuse Jeremiah of doing?
options: Weakening the hands of the men of war
questions.correctAnswer: Weakening the hands of the men of war
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 38:4 describes how the princes claimed Jeremiah weakened the hands of the men of war by his words.

questions.question: The city shall be given into the hand of which army?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 38:3 states that the city shall be given into the hand of the king of Babylon's army, which refers to the Chaldeans.

questions.question: True or False: Zedekiah was able to stop the princes from putting Jeremiah to death.
questions.explanation: Zedekiah stated in Jeremiah 38:5 that he could not do anything against the princes, indicating he could not stop them.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah was cast into a dungeon.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 38:6 confirms that Jeremiah was cast into the dungeon of Malchiah.

questions.question: True or False: Ebedmelech was a soldier in the king's army.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 38:7 states that Ebedmelech was one of the eunuchs in the king's house, not a soldier.

questions.question: True or False: There was plenty of food in the city when Jeremiah was in the dungeon.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 38:9 states that there was no more bread in the city, indicating a lack of food.

medium.title: Jeremiah Chapter 38 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Jeremiah Chapter 38 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Ebedmelech use to help Jeremiah out of the dungeon?
options: Old cast clouts and old rotten rags
questions.correctAnswer: Old cast clouts and old rotten rags
questions.explanation: Ebedmelech took old cast clouts and old rotten rags to let down by cords into the dungeon to Jeremiah. (Jeremiah 38:11)

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 38:17 promise will happen if Zedekiah goes forth to the king of Babylon's princes?
options: He will be put to death
His soul shall live and the city shall not be burned
questions.correctAnswer: His soul shall live and the city shall not be burned
questions.explanation: Jeremiah promises that if Zedekiah goes forth, his soul shall live and the city shall not be burned with fire. (Jeremiah 38:17)

questions.question: What did Zedekiah fear would happen if he obeyed Jeremiah's counsel?
options: He would be mocked by the Chaldeans
He would be praised by the people
questions.correctAnswer: He would be mocked by the Chaldeans
questions.explanation: Zedekiah expressed fear of being mocked by the Jews who had fallen to the Chaldeans if he obeyed. (Jeremiah 38:19)

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 38:18 warn will happen if Zedekiah does not go forth to the king of Babylon's princes?
options: The city will be given into the hands of the Chaldeans
He will be welcomed by the Chaldeans
questions.correctAnswer: The city will be given into the hands of the Chaldeans
questions.explanation: Jeremiah warns that if Zedekiah does not go forth, the city shall be given into the hand of the Chaldeans. (Jeremiah 38:18)

questions.question: Who was Ebedmelech in relation to the king?
questions.explanation: Ebedmelech was one of the eunuchs which was in the king's house. (Jeremiah 38:7)

questions.question: What did Zedekiah promise to Jeremiah in secret?
options: He would allow him to leave the city
He would not put him to death
questions.correctAnswer: He would not put him to death
questions.explanation: Zedekiah swore to Jeremiah that he would not put him to death or give him into the hands of those seeking his life. (Jeremiah 38:16)

questions.question: What did Ebedmelech tell the king about Jeremiah's condition?
options: He was in danger of dying from hunger
questions.correctAnswer: He was in danger of dying from hunger
questions.explanation: Ebedmelech informed the king that Jeremiah was likely to die for hunger in the dungeon where he was cast. (Jeremiah 38:9)

questions.question: What did Zedekiah say at the beginning of his conversation with Jeremiah?
options: I will not listen to you
I will ask thee a thing; hide nothing from me
questions.correctAnswer: I will ask thee a thing; hide nothing from me
questions.explanation: Zedekiah stated that he would ask Jeremiah a question and requested that he hide nothing from him. (Jeremiah 38:14)

questions.question: What did Jeremiah ask Zedekiah regarding his willingness to accept advice?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah questioned Zedekiah about whether he would listen if he declared the advice to him. (Jeremiah 38:15)

questions.question: What did Jeremiah encourage Zedekiah to obey?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah urged Zedekiah to obey the voice of the LORD, assuring him it would be well for him. (Jeremiah 38:20)

questions.question: What was the condition of the dungeon where Jeremiah was kept?
questions.explanation: The dungeon where Jeremiah was cast had no water, but was full of mire, causing him to sink. (Jeremiah 38:6)

questions.question: What did the princes accuse Jeremiah of doing?
options: Weakening the hands of the men of war
questions.correctAnswer: Weakening the hands of the men of war
questions.explanation: The princes accused Jeremiah of weakening the resolve of the men of war and the people by his words. (Jeremiah 38:4)

questions.question: True or False: Zedekiah was willing to heed Jeremiah's counsel after their conversation.
questions.explanation: Zedekiah swore to Jeremiah that he would not put him to death and expressed a desire to hear his counsel. (Jeremiah 38:16)

questions.question: True or False: Ebedmelech acted without the king's approval when he helped Jeremiah.
questions.explanation: Ebedmelech received a command from the king to take men and help Jeremiah out of the dungeon. (Jeremiah 38:10)

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah was taken out of the dungeon immediately after Ebedmelech's intervention.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah was drawn up from the dungeon after Ebedmelech's intervention, but remained in the court of the prison. (Jeremiah 38:13)

hard.title: Jeremiah Chapter 38 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Jeremiah Chapter 38.

questions.question: What will happen if Zedekiah refuses to go forth as Jeremiah advised?
options: He will be taken by the king of Babylon
He will be victorious over the Chaldeans
He will be honored in Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: He will be taken by the king of Babylon
questions.explanation: This is stated in Jeremiah 38:23, where it says he shall be taken by the king of Babylon.

questions.question: What will the women in the king of Judah's house say to the king of Babylon's princes?
options: Thy friends have set thee on
questions.correctAnswer: Thy friends have set thee on
questions.explanation: This is found in Jeremiah 38:22, where it mentions the women saying, 'Thy friends have set thee on.'

questions.question: What does Jeremiah tell Zedekiah he must do to save his life?
options: Go forth to the king of Babylon's princes
questions.correctAnswer: Go forth to the king of Babylon's princes
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 38:17 states that Zedekiah must go forth to the king of Babylon's princes to save his life.

questions.question: What does Zedekiah fear about going forth to the Chaldeans?
options: He will be mocked by the Chaldeans
He will be taken captive by his own people
questions.correctAnswer: He will be mocked by the Chaldeans
questions.explanation: Zedekiah expresses his fear of being mocked in Jeremiah 38:19, fearing what the Jews who have fallen to the Chaldeans might do.

questions.question: What did Zedekiah instruct Jeremiah to keep secret?
options: The words Jeremiah spoke to him
questions.correctAnswer: The words Jeremiah spoke to him
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 38:24, Zedekiah tells Jeremiah to let no man know of the words they spoke, ensuring his safety.

questions.question: What was Jeremiah’s condition while in the dungeon?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 38:6 describes how Jeremiah was let down into a dungeon where there was no water but mire.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'mire' in Jeremiah 38:6 mean?
questions.explanation: The word 'mire' refers to a muddy place, emphasizing Jeremiah's dire physical condition.

questions.question: Which literary device is used in Jeremiah 38:22 when the women speak to the king of Babylon's princes?
questions.explanation: The statement is ironic as the women will highlight the betrayal of Zedekiah's friends, turning his situation against him.

questions.question: Which Bible passage connects to Jeremiah 38:23's theme of captivity and destruction?
questions.explanation: Lamentations 1:8 speaks about the desolation of Jerusalem, echoing the theme of destruction mentioned in Jeremiah 38:23.

questions.question: Which passage connects with the warning to Zedekiah in Jeremiah 38:18 about the fate of the city?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:21 warns about the coming destruction, similar to the warnings given to Zedekiah in Jeremiah 38:18.

questions.question: What verse immediately precedes Jeremiah 38:24?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 38:23 speaks about the fate of Zedekiah's family, which directly precedes the instruction given in Jeremiah 38:24.

questions.question: What does Zedekiah say to Jeremiah in Jeremiah 38:25?
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 38:25, Zedekiah expresses his concern about their discussion being revealed to the princes.

questions.question: Jeremiah remained in the court of the prison until when?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 38:28 states that he remained there until the day that Jerusalem was taken.

questions.question: True or False: Zedekiah openly proclaimed his fears to Jeremiah regarding the Chaldeans.
questions.explanation: Zedekiah openly expressed his fear in Jeremiah 38:19, showing his concerns about the Jews who had fallen to the Chaldeans.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah was released from prison before the fall of Jerusalem.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah remained in the court of the prison until Jerusalem was taken, as stated in Jeremiah 38:28.

theological.title: Jeremiah Chapter 38 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Jeremiah Chapter 38 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Jeremiah 38:2 teach about God's sovereign judgment and mercy?
options: God sovereignly judges the unrepentant but offers mercy to those who submit
God punishes all inhabitants equally without distinction
God's mercy is unconditional regardless of human response
Human efforts can override divine judgment
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly judges the unrepentant but offers mercy to those who submit
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 38:2 teaches that those who remain in the city will die by sword, famine, and pestilence (judgment), but those who go to the Chaldeans will live, showing God's sovereign judgment coupled with mercy to those who obey.

questions.question: What doctrine about the consequences of rejecting prophetic warning is taught in Jeremiah 38:4?
options: Rejecting God's messenger weakens the community and brings judgment
Prophetic words are always politically motivated and should be ignored
The people have no responsibility for their leaders' decisions
Prophets only bring encouragement and never judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Rejecting God's messenger weakens the community and brings judgment
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 38:4 shows that the princes viewed Jeremiah's words as weakening the warriors and people, indicating that rejecting God's prophetic warning leads to communal weakening and judgment.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine protection of His servants is evident in Jeremiah 38:10?
options: God uses human agents to preserve His prophets' lives
God abandons His servants to suffer without aid
Divine protection is automatic and requires no human action
God does not intervene in political affairs
questions.correctAnswer: God uses human agents to preserve His prophets' lives
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 38:10 shows that the king commands Ebedmelech to rescue Jeremiah, demonstrating that God providentially uses human agents to protect His servants.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Jeremiah 38:3 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 38:3 declares that the city will be given into the hand of the Babylonian king’s army, demonstrating God's sovereignty over nations and events.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is especially highlighted in Jeremiah 38:16?
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 38:16, Zedekiah swears by the LORD that he will not put Jeremiah to death nor deliver him to his enemies, manifesting God's faithfulness through the king’s oath.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 38 prepare for the fulfillment of God's judgment theme in the exile narrative?
options: By showing the inevitability of Jerusalem’s fall due to disobedience
By predicting the immediate restoration of Israel
By promising political victory over Babylon
By emphasizing military strategy over prophecy
questions.correctAnswer: By showing the inevitability of Jerusalem’s fall due to disobedience
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 38 outlines the unavoidable judgment and fall of Jerusalem, preparing for the exile theme seen in later biblical history.

questions.question: Which redemptive-historical theme is connected to Jeremiah 38:17-18?
options: The call to repentance and trust in God's salvation
The promise of an immediate earthly kingdom
The rejection of all foreign alliances
questions.correctAnswer: The call to repentance and trust in God's salvation
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 38:17-18 calls Zedekiah to go to Babylon to save his life and the city, reflecting the biblical theme of repentance and trust in God’s appointed means of salvation.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Jeremiah 38:6 and 38:13 teach about divine providence and human suffering?
options: God allows suffering but provides deliverance through human agency
Suffering is meaningless and without divine purpose
Deliverance is guaranteed without any suffering
questions.correctAnswer: God allows suffering but provides deliverance through human agency
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 38:6 shows Jeremiah suffering in a mire-filled dungeon, and 38:13 shows his rescue by Ebedmelech, teaching that God permits suffering but also providentially provides rescue through others.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about fear and faithfulness do Jeremiah 38:19 and 38:20 teach?
options: Fear can hinder obedience, but faithfulness to God leads to deliverance
Fear is the ultimate guide for decision-making
Faithfulness does not require overcoming fear
Obedience is irrelevant to God’s promises
questions.correctAnswer: Fear can hinder obedience, but faithfulness to God leads to deliverance
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 38:19 records Zedekiah’s fear of the Jews, while 38:20 urges obedience to God’s voice for well-being, illustrating the tension between fear and faithfulness.

questions.question: What doctrine about prophetic confidentiality and political intrigue is taught by Jeremiah 38:24-27?
options: Prophetic messages may be kept secret to protect the prophet
Prophetic messages must always be public regardless of circumstances
Prophets have no role in political affairs
questions.correctAnswer: Prophetic messages may be kept secret to protect the prophet
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 38:24-27 shows the king instructing Jeremiah to keep his words secret from the princes to avoid danger, teaching that prophetic confidentiality can be necessary amidst political threats.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Jeremiah 38:6-13 shows God as indifferent to human suffering. What does these verses actually teach?
options: God allows suffering but provides human means for rescue and preservation
God causes suffering without any intention of relief
God is absent from human affairs
Suffering is a sign of divine abandonment
questions.correctAnswer: God allows suffering but provides human means for rescue and preservation
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 38:6-13 shows Jeremiah suffering in a dungeon but being rescued by Ebedmelech, demonstrating God’s providential care through human instruments, not indifference.

questions.question: What doctrine about human agency and divine sovereignty is taught in Jeremiah 38:7-9?
options: God uses human advocacy to intervene in divine plans
Humans act independently of God’s will
Divine plans are fixed and exclude human participation
Human actions are irrelevant to divine outcomes
questions.correctAnswer: God uses human advocacy to intervene in divine plans
questions.explanation: Ebedmelech’s intervention (Jeremiah 38:7-9) shows that God sovereignly incorporates human advocacy and action within His plans.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is especially demonstrated by God's word through Jeremiah in 38:22-23?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 38:22-23 foretells the coming disgrace and captivity of the king’s family, showing God’s all-knowing nature foretelling future events accurately.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about divine judgment and covenant responsibility is taught by Jeremiah 38:1 and 38:28?
options: Ignoring God’s covenant leads to inevitable judgment and captivity
God’s covenant guarantees earthly prosperity regardless of obedience
Judgment is unrelated to covenant faithfulness
The prophet’s role is only to encourage, not to warn
questions.correctAnswer: Ignoring God’s covenant leads to inevitable judgment and captivity
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 38:1 warns of judgment for those in the city, and 38:28 shows Jeremiah present at Jerusalem’s fall, confirming covenant disobedience leads to judgment.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 38:14-16 illustrate the theological tension between divine revelation and human fear?
options: Divine revelation demands faith despite human fear of consequences
Divine revelation is always comforting and never challenging
Prophets should avoid revealing difficult truths
questions.correctAnswer: Divine revelation demands faith despite human fear of consequences
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 38:14-16 shows Zedekiah fearing Jeremiah’s words but swearing to protect him, illustrating the tension between fear and trust in God’s word.
